description:
As a site reliability engineer, you want to monitor the frequency of uptime check results for your web servers. You have a log file named /home/user/monitoring/uptime_checks.log containing the uptime status of three servers: web01, web02, and web03. Each line in this log file records a timestamp (in the format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS), the server name, and the status ("UP" or "DOWN"), separated by spaces. Your task is to:
  1. Navigate to the /home/user/monitoring directory and verify the existence of the uptime_checks.log file.
  2. Process uptime_checks.log to count the number of times each server is reported as "UP" and as "DOWN". This means you need to count the number of lines that have each combination of server and status.
  3. Create a summary log file named /home/user/monitoring/uptime_summary.log. Each line in this summary log must contain: server name, status, and the count, separated by spaces.
  4. Sort the entries in uptime_summary.log in ascending order first by server name, then by status ("DOWN" before "UP"), for each server.
Required Output Format: 
web01 DOWN 
web01 UP 
web02 DOWN 
web02 UP 
web03 DOWN 
web03 UP
Where is an integer count for each status per server. After completing the summary, display the contents of uptime_summary.log to confirm the result.

After the agent completes the task, the following file will exist:

File: /home/user/monitoring/uptime_summary.log
Contents:
web01 DOWN 2
web01 UP 2
web02 DOWN 1
web02 UP 1
web03 DOWN 1
web03 UP 2

The directory /home/user/monitoring will be writable by the agent, and both log files will have permissions set to allow full read/write access for the agent ("user"). The agent will be able to display the contents of /home/user/monitoring/uptime_summary.log in the terminal for verification.
